page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance from the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon Platinum 6149 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. Hardware resources include 4 physical cores mapped across 8 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is not bundled locally, necessitating network-attached block devices, and network throughput is provisioned at a baseline of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor includes AVX-512 and AES instruction sets, but lacks newer extensions such as AMX, VNNI, or built-in accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes show mid-tier performance across multi-threaded computational workloads, supported by an aggregate PassMark CPU score of 8,280.79 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 7,203.49. Instruction-heavy tasks such as Clang compilation (6,770.0) and ray tracing (6,039.0) land in the middle tier. In contrast, single-threaded processing reflects architectural age, with single-core Geekbench (1,091.0) and stress-ng (1,355.68) tests scoring in the lower quartile. In-memory throughput is mixed; cached small-block read bandwidth reaches 402.4 GB/sec and Redis SET operations attain 7.08 million ops/sec, but uncached read bandwidth drops to 38.98 GB/sec.

Without local NVMe storage and limited to 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, ecs.hfc5.2xlarge faces bottlenecks in I/O-intensive database and heavy web-serving roles, where static web throughput reaches only 4.68 GB/sec. Large model LLM inference is also severely constrained due to memory limits and the lack of a GPU accelerator, evidenced by a 7B model token generation rate of 4.86 tokens/sec. The instance represents an economical, compute-oriented allocation for distributed compute tasks, batch builds, CI/CD pipelines, and application backends requiring fixed core allocations and modest memory footprints.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.2xlarge is a compute-focused instance featuring an Intel Xeon Platinum 6149 processor running at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. It lacks local storage and bundled GPUs, relying on external storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks place its multi-core capabilities in the mid-range with a PassMark CPU score of 8,280.79, while single-threaded speed and uncached memory operations score in lower tiers. Memory performance remains stable for cached operations, recording 7.08 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking local drives or specialized AI accelerators, this configuration is best deployed for CI/CD compilation, batch compute routines, and lightweight containerized application workloads.
